dedupe_keys.name: arpa e grid optimization go competition data sets

description: These data sets hold the synthetic power system cases, problem descriptions and team results of the ARPA-E Grid Optimization (GO) Competition, run to find and fairly test new methods for hard power grid optimisation problems. They were published in 2024 on the DOE Open Energy Data Initiative by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, with Stephen Elbert, Jesse Holzer, Arun Veeramany, Kory Hedman, Hans Mittelmann, Carleton Coffrin, Thomas Overbye, Adam Birchfield and others as creators. Challenge 1 (2018 to 2019) posed single-period security-constrained AC optimal power flow, with network models of different sizes and operating scenarios covering demand, renewables and generator and line availability, mostly synthetic from the ARPA-E GRID DATA program. Challenge 3 posed multiperiod market problems with advisory models for extreme weather events, day-ahead and real-time markets; Event 4 alone had 591 synthetic scenarios on nine network models. Format descriptions and code to validate data and solutions are included; Challenge 2 is also listed. Coverage is synthetic US-scale grids. Files are downloadable from OEDI as publicly accessible submissions at no cost. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0. Simulation uses are benchmarking optimal power flow and contingency solvers. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day. The underlying files were not downloaded, so their contents are not verified here.
